chapter: New Orleans bands, Louis and the Lyric
title: Drummers who influenced him: Louis Cottrell and Paul Detroit
summary: Zutty names Louis Cottrell Sr. and Paul Detroit as his models, admiring their tone and tuning; he says Paul Barbarin was just ahead of him and mentions Henry Martin.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well I was going to ask you now what drummers influenced you? If any.
Two guys. Louis Cotrell and Paul Detroit.
Paul Detroit.
Yes, Paul Detroit. Paul played at the Orpheum Theater under old man Tasso, who was the conductor.
How do you spell that? (Tasca)?
(Tasca).
Yes, okay don't worry, I can check that out. Don't worry. And the other one?
The other one was Louis Cotrell. That's when Steve Louis was playing with Piren at Spanish Forte for Tranchina's.
Well is that Louis Cotrell a relation of the clarinet player?
That's right. That's his father.
Oh!
Yes, that's his father. Old man Louis Cotrell noted for his ( ) work. I used to, Steve used to bring me out there to

TRANCHINA'S (Trombonist) and I'd sit right beside old man Cotrell and he never did ask me to play. He would just look at me just to see was I watching what he was doing. Listening and watching, see? And that's all. I always admired him and Paul Detroit. He played with Frankie (Fordwith's?) father.
Yes?
Yes. Because they were....
Well I thought Paul Detroit was in California.
Huh?
In California? Was that Paul Detroit?
Yes, sure. ( ?).
And his wife wanted Zuddy to take any of the drums that he wanted.
Well let's think, (of course) so Baby Dodds. Now Paul Barbarin, would he be around at this time?
Well Paul was just ahead of me.
Ahead of you?
Just a little ahead of me.
Oh, I see. And he wasn't an influence?
No. I called my tune.
Yes, you named your tune.
Because I liked the way that the other guys played. Henry Martin, he was a left handed drummer.
Yes.
He played with Kid Ory's band. He was very good.
Well I mean I suppose when you named those two, those are your major influences, but everybody can hear something in somebody else which is interesting.

That was my man. Yes. Paul Detroit, because I used to like to hear, I'd get him at the theater in time to hear him come out and tune up his drums, you know. He used to sound so good. That big bass drum used to sound so good.
Well Zutty, of course they were like inspirations or influences, whatever you call them. But I mean your own thing was not like theirs.
No, it was a little different. It's a little different, but they had a tone of drum that
I liked so much.
Yes, I see what you mean.

They knew how to tune their drums up, you know. Like old man Louis Catrell Catrell used to have a roll that was just like tissue paper. A bucket full of shots, you know. And that's why I loved him and I went to Lyric, to the Orphum, those acts (?) Theater the year Paul Detroit played (Cezars?), see?
